newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Dos Bocas remains shut, could open soon.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Dos Bocas remains shut, could open soon.

text.p: Mexican crude port Dos Bocas in Tabasco state remained closed Tuesday morning with three crude tankers waiting to sail, a port official said.
The official, who declined to be named, said the port could be opened in the morning if choppy waves relax.
"It could be opened between 10 and 12 a.m., when we expect waves to fall to eight feet high, but for the moment the waves are pretty strong," he said.

The second largest of Mexico's main three crude ports shut on Sunday at 2200 local/0300 GMT as a storm front hit the region. The official said Tuesday morning that waves were still 10 feet high, with winds between 20 and 25 km per hour.

He said the waiting ships were named Tromso Confident, Rich Duck and Magnolia. One of the tankers held a contracted one million barrels of light Isthmus crude, another held 500,000 barrels of heavy Maya and the third held 250,000 barrels of Maya and 250,000 barrels of extra-light Olmeca, he added.
Dos Bocas exported an average of 505,900 barrels per day (bpd) in 1996, Pajaritos exported an average 416,200 bpd and Cayo Arcas shipped about 576,300 bpd, according to the latest Pemex figures.
